name: CUPID
summary: CUPID is the proposed successor to CUORE, using enriched lithium-molybdate scintillating bolometers to search for molybdenum-100 neutrinoless double-beta decay. Its design combines the existing CUORE cryogenic infrastructure with particle identification.
detection_principle: Each crystal provides a heat measurement and a separate scintillation-light signal. The heat-to-light response identifies alpha backgrounds, while the summed decay energy tests for a narrow neutrinoless-decay peak.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
